page: Amazon Web Services r8idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, providing 64 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 32 physical cores with multithreading. Memory allocation is scaled to 512.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for dense data applications.

For localized input and output demands, the instance integrates 3800 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. High-throughput data movement is further supported by a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators, prioritizing raw memory bandwidth and fast local block storage access.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of paired RAM, dedicated physical compute cores, and included high-capacity NVMe drive space within a single node, which reduces reliance on external network-attached volumes for temporary and scratch workloads. The primary operational tradeoff involves the ephemeral nature of the bundled local storage, requiring application-level data redundancy.

Given its heavy memory footprint, baseline 100 Gbps network, and direct NVMe storage, the instance fits in-memory databases, real-time caching fleets, distributed stream processing, and large transactional database engines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered for data-heavy enterprise workloads. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs from 32 physical Intel x86_64 cores operating at 3.9 GHz, paired with 512.0 GB of system memory. Hardware resources include 3800 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network interface speed of 100 Gbps, with zero integrated GPUs. The instance balances dense computational power with an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory capacity and high-throughput local disk storage. This hardware layout provides qualitative cost efficiency by avoiding external storage IOPS bottlenecks for high-frequency operations, though it requires architectures resilient to the transient state of local instance store volumes. The r8idn.16xlarge is well configured for in-memory databases, large-scale distributed analytics, high-volume transactional workloads, and low-latency data processing pipelines.
